name: Anger & Irritation
description: Pattern related to sudden frustration, emotional reactivity, or heightened physical tension.
safetyGuidance: This is not a clinical diagnosis. Informational pattern match based on reported frustration and tension.

solutions.title: Anger Breathing
solutions.purpose: Create a short pause and breathing reset before reacting.
instructions: Inhale deeply through your nose for 4 counts.
Exhale forcefully through pursed lips for 6 counts.
Visualize blowing out heat and pressure with each long exhale.
Repeat until your heart rate slows down.

solutions.title: Pause-and-Reset
solutions.purpose: Provide a short structured pause before responding to a triggering situation.
instructions: Step physically back from the immediate situation.
Do not send messages, speak, or react while the timer runs.
Breathe deeply and count backward from 60.
Ask yourself: 'Will reacting right now help or hurt my long-term peace?'

solutions.title: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
instructions: Clench your jaw tight for 5 seconds, then unclench completely.
Squeeze your fists tight for 5 seconds, then open palms wide.
Tense your abdomen tight, then let it loosen.
Notice the cooling sensation as muscle tightness melts away.

solutions.title: Mind-Clearing Exercise
solutions.purpose: Provide a short period to step away mentally from the immediate irritation.
instructions: Sit in a cool, quiet spot.
Close your eyes and focus on a neutral mental image (cold water, falling snow).
Let hot thoughts pass without holding onto them.
Remain quiet until the session finishes.

solutions.title: Guided Meditation
solutions.purpose: Provide a short calming mindfulness activity.
instructions: Acknowledge anger as an energetic warning signal, not an absolute command.
Breathe calmly into your chest and belly.
Choose composure over conflict for your own peace of mind.
